A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAMBA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model training, downstream evaluations, perplexity and throughput measurements, retrieval experiments, and architecture analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds architecture ablations, Phonebook experiments, and downstream evaluations.

M1.justification: SAMBA retains the same Mamba–MLP–SWA–MLP arrangement, Mamba computations, 2,048-token attention window, and SwiGLU components. Additional comparator variants and post-training configurations do not revise the proposed architecture or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds multi-key retrieval and cross-task transfer scenarios through Phonebook, discourse word prediction through LAMBADA, and harder knowledge/reasoning evaluations through MMLU-Pro and GPQA. Earlier training corpora and evaluation tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Mega-S6, Mamba-SWA-MLP, MLP2-SWA-MLP, and SAMBA-NoPE to the existing SlimPajama comparison. The new chat evaluation in Table 8 includes Phi3 (June), R-Gemma 9B, FalconMamba, Jamba-1.5-Mini, and Llama-3.1/3.2 instruction models, substantially expanding evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 100-step Phonebook fine-tuning at 4K length, testing over 20–480 name-number pairs, and evaluation of transfer from passkey tuning. It also adds the June post-training configuration and benchmark-specific chat evaluation protocols. Sliding RetNet's reported small-model size changes from 438M to 446M; this alone does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New ablations test replacing Mamba with MLPs, removing RoPE, and alternative hybridization arrangements at two scales. Phonebook additionally tests memory load and transfer of passkey-trained retrieval skills. Earlier context-length, full-attention, attention-head, and short-convolution analyses are retained, including material moved to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report throughput averaged over 10 measurements and approximately ±0.3% perplexity fluctuation. Neither introduces new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance testing, or repeated-run uncertainty procedures; additional result rows use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3, 4, and 8 and the Phonebook curves in Figure 4. For example, the new 1.3B SAMBA-NoPE result has 326.17 perplexity at 16,384 tokens versus SAMBA's retained 6.96, and the June chat evaluation reports averages of 66.1 for SAMBA and 64.4 for Phi3. Original base-model, preview-model, and other retained scores are unchanged; June results concern a separate post-training configuration.

T1.justification: The mathematical description of Mamba and the attention/selection entropy definitions are unchanged. The entropy material moves from Appendix C to Appendix E; no substantive theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central claim of an efficient hybrid with strong language modeling and length extrapolation remains. v2 adds a headline claim of superior Phonebook retrieval extrapolation, explicitly claims first-at-scale hybrid superiority, and clarifies the distinction between zero-shot perplexity extrapolation and fine-tuned recall. The introduction qualifies infinite extrapolation as potential.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability boundaries through failed passkey-to-Phonebook transfer and an explicit perplexity-versus-retrieval extrapolation trade-off. It adds explanations involving Mamba's contribution and hybrid I/O/cache costs, and explicitly restricts fair architecture comparisons to matched-data models in Tables 7–8. The original base-model retrieval and task-dependent performance limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies RoPE's 10,000 base frequency and documents the existing summarization evaluation's ZeroSCROLLS source, tokenizer, document-length statistics, greedy decoding, and generation limits in Appendix F. It describes implementation choices for added comparators and changes the code-availability statement from a sample implementation to open-data training code. Existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A new related-work appendix substantially expands positioning across hybrid recurrent models, sparse attention, and length extrapolation. It identifies Griffin as the closest architecture and distinguishes SAMBA from Griffin, Infini-Attention, Megalodon, and other approaches. These substantive comparisons go beyond the accompanying citation-style and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: instruction-tuned results lead Section 3.1, base-model results move to Appendix B, retrieval experiments are consolidated in Section 3.4, and selected analyses move to Appendix D. The abstract and introduction are revised, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated evaluation, analysis, implementation, and related-work sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds two evaluation tables and the Phonebook figure, expands Table 3, and substantially rearranges existing displays. The introductory performance figure moves into Section 3.3, prompt throughput moves to the appendix, and several tables change main-text/appendix placement. The document also adopts a different title, heading, and page-header layout.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in architectural attribution and retrieval generalization: Table 3 directly tests Mamba removal and positional encoding, while Figure 4 tests multi-item retrieval and exposes poor cross-task transfer. These controls, clearer comparison qualifications, substantive positioning against Griffin, and newly documented summarization procedures substantially strengthen the central empirical argument. Phonebook comparisons still mix model sizes and tuning conditions, and uncertainty reporting remains limited, but the added evidence materially clarifies both the architecture's benefits and its boundaries.
